Running a marketing agency without the right project management tool means missed deadlines, confused clients, and chaos that keeps compounding. Here are the seven best options to fix that in 2026.

In this video, George Vlasyev breaks down the seven best project management tools for marketing agencies in 2026, covering ClickUp, Monday.com, Scoro, Asana, Productive, Wrike, and ProofHub across features, pricing, and which type of agency each one is actually built for.

💡 About The Video:
Marketing agencies deal with a specific kind of operational chaos — campaigns running in parallel, client feedback loops, content calendars, resource bottlenecks, and billing all happening at once. Generic task managers built for software teams or solo users rarely hold up under that pressure. This video covers seven tools that are genuinely worth considering for agency work in 2026, with honest breakdowns of what each one does well and where it falls short. ClickUp is the most complete option, with customizable dashboards, multiple views, time tracking, forms for creative briefs, and paid plans starting at $7 per user per month. Monday.com excels at visual planning and automation, making it easy to keep internal teams and clients aligned, starting at $9 per user per month. Scoro and Productive both go beyond task management to offer full business visibility including invoicing, profitability reporting, CRM, and resource planning, making them strong choices for mid-size to larger agencies that want one system across operations and financials.

Asana is the cleanest option for straightforward campaign planning and content scheduling, with built-in time tracking on advanced plans and paid tiers starting at $10.99 per user per month. Wrike handles complex approval workflows well with built-in feedback on images and videos and custom approval chains, starting at $10 per user per month. ProofHub is the most focused creative tool on the list, with a built-in proofing feature for reviewing and approving assets without email threads, flat pricing starting at $45 per month for unlimited users regardless of team size.

ClickUp checks the most boxes for most agencies and is the strongest all-around recommendation, but the right tool depends on whether your priority is visual planning, financial visibility, creative proofing, or task simplicity. In this video, George Vlasyev breaks down the six best project management tools for small businesses in 2026, covering ClickUp, Trello, Asana, Basecamp, Slack, and Monday.com across features, pricing, ease of use, and which type of team each one is actually built for.

🌐 Visit my official website for systems, templates, and services: https://vlasyev.com
🎥 Work with me: https://vlasyev.com

🕒 Timestamps:
00:00 Intro
00:53 ClickUp
02:06 Trello
03:20 Asana
04:24 Basecamp
05:37 Slack
06:41 Monday.com
07:59 Final Thoughts

💡 About The Video:
Finding the best project management software for a small business is harder than it looks because the right answer depends entirely on how your team works. This video covers six of the most widely used tools and gives you a clear, honest breakdown of what each one is actually good at. ClickUp is the most complete option on the list, replacing multiple tools with tasks, docs, chat, goals, dashboards, Gantt charts, and automations in one place, with a free plan that includes unlimited tasks and users. Trello keeps things visual and minimal with its card and board system, generous free plan, and near-zero learning curve. Asana adds structure with list, board, and calendar views plus recurring tasks and milestone tracking, free for up to 15 users. Basecamp takes a different approach entirely, combining to-do lists, message boards, file storage, group chat, and automatic check-ins into one hub designed to reduce app switching. Slack is primarily a communication tool but functions well as lightweight project management when paired with integrations like Trello or Asana. Monday.com rounds out the list with its highly customizable templates, multiple views, and automation rules, though its free plan is limited to two users.

Every tool on this list has a genuine use case, but they are not interchangeable. Trello is the right call for teams that want a simple visual board and nothing else. Asana works well for teams that need recurring task structures and milestone tracking without a steep setup. Basecamp suits teams that want communication and task management in one place without deep customization. Slack belongs in the stack as a communication layer, not a standalone project manager. Monday.com fits teams that want visual, highly customizable workflows and can invest time in setup. ClickUp is the strongest all-around choice for small businesses that want one platform to handle everything and room to scale without switching tools.
